title: Lay the photo scale beside a find on the floor of its cut
instruction: Get the find ready for its record photograph. Put the trowel back in the orange tool tray, then lay the 10 cm scale flat on the floor of the cut beside the find, centred alongside it, parallel to it and 1 to 4 cm from it. Leave the find exactly where it lies. When you are done, let go and move both arms back, clear of the cut and out of the photo.
context: Archaeological excavation recording (O*NET 19-3091.02 Archeologists: record the exact locations and conditions of artifacts, using drawings and photographs; field technicians and site supervisors do it many times a day). Before a find is lifted it is photographed where it lies: tools and hands come out of the shot, and a scale goes beside the find, parallel to it, flat on the same surface the find lies on, and not touching it. The find is never moved, because where it lies is part of the record. A scale left on the ground surface above a sunken cut is nearer the camera than the find, so it reads too large: here the cut is 40 mm deep and the camera about 0.94 m up, about 4%; in a 0.5 m grave cut shot from a 2 m pole, about 25%. Here the trowel lies on the very strip where the scale belongs, and the tool tray is within reach of one arm only, the photo kit of the other only.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Six things are on the table, nothing else. (1) Ground surface: four light-brown painted pine blocks, each 40 mm tall, fixed to the table as a square frame round a sunken cut, outer 300 x 300 mm, centred at x 26.0 cm, y 0. Near bank x 11-17 cm, y -15 to +15 cm (60 x 300 mm); far bank x 35-41 cm, same y; left bank y +9 to +15 cm, x 17-35 cm (180 x 60 mm); right bank y -15 to -9 cm, same x. The cut opening is x 17-35 cm, y -9 to +9 cm (180 x 180 mm); its floor is the table top, 40 mm below the ground surface. (2) Find: a loose cream 3D-printed PLA block standing in for a worked bone point, 90 x 26 x 16 mm (16 mm tall), 35 g, flat on the cut floor, centred at x 26.5 cm, y +5.0 cm, its long axis turned 20 degrees from +x toward +y; its corners are at (x, y) (30.28, 7.76), (31.17, 5.32), (22.72, 2.24) and (21.83, 4.68) cm (a real build marks its long centre line and centre on its top). Its +y long side is 12-43 mm from the left bank. (3) Trowel: a loose grey HDPE block standing in for an archaeologist's pointing trowel, 140 x 40 x 18 mm (18 mm tall), 90 g, its handle end the -x end (toward the robot); flat on the cut floor, centred at x 25.43 cm, y -0.82 cm, long axis at 20 degrees: parallel to the find and 18 mm from its -y long side along its whole length, on the strip where the scale belongs. Its corners are at (31.32, 3.45), (32.69, -0.31), (19.54, -5.09) and (18.17, -1.34) cm; its handle end is 12 mm from the near bank. (4) Tool tray: an open orange plastic tray fixed to the table, outer 190 x 140 mm, centred at x 25.0 cm, y -36.0 cm, with a 10 mm thick floor and 5 mm walls rising to 30 mm above the table; inside 180 x 130 mm (x 16-34 cm, y -42.5 to -29.5 cm). (5) Photo-kit box: an open dark-grey plastic tray fixed to the table, outer 150 x 100 mm, centred at x 25.0 cm, y +33.0 cm, with a 5 mm floor and 5 mm walls rising to 15 mm; inside 140 x 90 mm. (6) Scale: a loose white painted hardwood bar standing in for a 10 cm photographic scale, 100 x 20 x 15 mm (15 mm tall), 25 g, flat on the kit box's floor, centred at x 25.0 cm, y +33.0 cm, its long axis along x (a real build paints 1 cm black bands and a centre mark on both 100 x 20 mm faces, so either face can be up). Gripping from above, only the right arm reaches the tool tray and only the left arm the photo-kit box.
scoring: Every control step the scorer reads the find's, trowel's and scale's poses, each gripper's tool point (TCP) and opening (0 closed, 1 open, pads 94 mm apart). 'Find frame': u along the find's long axis, n square to it, seen from above. The find's reference is its pose at the first control step. 'Disturbed': at any step the find's centre is more than 5 mm (horizontally) from its reference, it has turned (heading) or tilted more than 3 deg, or its bottom is more than 3 mm above the cut floor. 'Rests on the find': the scale's or the trowel's outline seen from above overlaps the find's, and that object's bottom is less than 21 mm above the cut floor. 'On the floor': the scale's bottom within 3 mm of the cut floor, its 15 mm axis within 5 deg of vertical (either big face down), and its whole outline seen from above inside the cut opening (2 mm slack). 'a' is the angle seen from above between the scale's long axis and the find's, folded to 0-90 deg; 'g' is the distance from the scale's centre to the find's long centre line, along n, minus 23 mm (13 + 10 mm half-widths: the edge gap if parallel); 's' is the distance from the find's centre to the scale's centre along u. 'Tight': on the floor, a 5 deg or less, g 10 to 40 mm, s 25 mm or less, its and the find's outlines not overlapping. 'Rough': on the floor, a 12 deg or less, g 5 to 50 mm, s 45 mm or less, not overlapping (tight is also rough). 'Stowed': the trowel's centre inside the tray's inner outline (x 16-34 cm, y -42.5 to -29.5 cm) and its bottom within 5 mm of the tray floor. 'Hands clear': both grippers open 0.5 or more (pads 47 mm or more apart, wider than any loose part) and neither TCP, seen from above, at x 5 cm or more with y -21 to +21 cm (over the frame, within 60 mm of it, as open pads reach 56 mm from the TCP, or past its far side, the arm over it); grippers that cannot be read are not clear. Score 0 if the find was ever disturbed, if anything rests on the find, or if the hands are not clear. Otherwise: 1.0 if the scale is tight and the trowel stowed; 0.75 if the scale is rough but not tight and the trowel stowed; 0.5 if the scale is tight or rough and the trowel not stowed; 0.25 if the trowel is stowed and the scale neither tight nor rough; 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step; the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions (hands clear included) have held for 1 s with the find, scale and trowel each within 3 mm of every position it had over the last 0.5 s. In a real trial: the trial video shows any lift, tilt or turn of the find during the trial; the tape marks at its corners give the final displacement and turn. In a top photo a steel rule, square from the centre mark on the scale's top to the centre line marked on the find, minus 23 mm, gives g; along that line from the find's centre mark to the foot of the square, s; the photo or a protractor gives a; a straightedge across the banks shows the scale's top 25 +/- 3 mm below it (on the floor); a rule gives the trowel's place in the tray; the last video frame against tape lines at the zone's edge gives the grippers.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one friction (the simulator's default). The scale is a 15 mm bar (real ones are 2-5 mm thick) so the gripper can hold it; plain white here, banded on both 100 x 20 mm faces in a real build, so either face up reads. The trowel is a plain block, gripped at its handle end. The find is a printed stand-in on a hard floor (on site it lies in soil). Camera parallax is not simulated: the scale's level is scored geometrically. Touching the find counts only through how far it moves.
reset_notes: Put the find back on its corner tape marks (centred at x 26.5 cm, y +5.0 cm, long axis at 20 degrees), the trowel back on its outline with its handle end toward the robot, and the scale back flat in the kit box, centred at x 25.0 cm, y +33.0 cm, along x. The frame, the tool tray and the kit box are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
